title: Ang 517–523: Gujri ki Var M5
tomorrow: what could a man offer God, if the calf already drank the milk?

cards: Watch a real fan at a game. It isn't just a feeling in the chest. It's the jersey, the chant in the throat, eyes locked on the field, the replay ringing in the ears all the way home.
The whole body has signed up. On ang 517, Guru Arjan's ballad in Gujri opens with that kind of love. Not a feeling tucked away somewhere.
Eyes, ears, tongue, and the inside too.

teach.b: So, one question: where does devotion live? Here's the first salok of the fifth Guru's ballad, in paraphrase.
Inside, worship the Guru; with the tongue, the jihva, repeat the Guru's Name. With the eyes, behold the Satguru, the True Guru; with the ears, hear the Guru's Name.
Dyed in the True Guru's love, one finds a place in the Lord's court. The answer is everywhere at once. Not inside instead of outside.
The whole person, turned one way. A neighbor tradition says something close, in its own words.

teach.h: A NEIGHBOR: ALL THY HEART AND MIGHT.
teach.b: In the Torah, in the passage Jews call the Shema, Deuteronomy says: "And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might." Heart, soul, might: the whole person again.
That's the shared thing, and it's real. Two scriptures, two peoples, asking for all of you, not a corner. And here's the honest difference.

The Shema is spoken to Israel, and the love it asks for is lived through the commandments God gives there. The salok turns the whole body toward the Guru and the Guru's Name, the Guru as the way to the One.
Same shape of love; a different center. Neither needs the other to be the same to be true to itself.

how: Gujri ki Var of Guru Arjan is sung in kirtan salok by salok and pauri by pauri; Sikhs reading the Granth in order reach it right after Guru Amar Das's var in the same raga.

o: where Guru Amar Das's ballad in Gujri begins
the page where the Bhagat Kabir's Gujri hymns start
where Guru Arjan's ballad in Gujri begins

p: all thy heart, soul and might

s: the first salok of Guru Arjan's Gujri ballad names the tongue, the eyes and the ears
inside, worship; the tongue repeats; the eyes behold; the ears hear the Guru's Name.
the Shema and this salok say exactly the same thing
both ask for the whole person; the Shema centers love lived through God's commandments, the salok the Guru and the Name.
in Sikh teaching, devotion is only a private feeling
the salok sends it through the tongue, the eyes and the ears as well as the inside.

games.q: your aunt says devotion is private, all in the heart. your uncle says it only counts if people can see it. by the salok on ang 517, what's missing from each?
o: each has only part: the salok asks for inside, tongue, eyes and ears together.
nothing from the aunt; the salok is about the inside alone.
nothing from the uncle; the salok is about what others can see.
games.why: the salok won't split it: inside, worship; the tongue repeats; the eyes behold; the ears hear. the whole person, turned one way.

practice: Walk through the salok with your senses, one at a time: let your eyes rest on one thing in the room, then let your ears find one sound.
Stay with that one sound for the rest of the sit, listening to it the way a fan listens to a chant. If you'd like, read the salok on ang 517, or the pauri on ang 518, first.

carryVoice: Hold on to the fifth's ballad: all of you, turned one way. Day fifteen-oh-four, with the whole body.
